exposure: Planned vaginal births (including assisted VBs and emergency C-sections)
outcome: Determinants of CSMR (e.g., maternal age, hospital type, mood disorders, birth attendant)
cohort: Low-risk pregnancies in Queensland, Australia, resulting in live or intrapartum stillbirth with >=20 gestational weeks and/or >=400 gm birth weight, from 2008 to 2017.
finding: The incidence of Caesarean section on maternal request (CSMR) increased 1.75-fold over 10 years in Australia and was influenced by factors such as advanced maternal age, private hospital delivery, and maternal mood disorders.
mod_finding: Compared to planned vaginal births, CSMR was associated with an increased risk of anaesthetic complications, neonatal morbidities, and special care admission, although it showed slightly reduced odds of birth asphyxia.
